text:
sara: Observed repeated tail-latency spikes from us-west inference pool starting ~08:12 UTC. Correlates with node gpu-wn-23. GPU0 temp jumping 85->98C and power cap oscillating 250W <-> 180W. Also saw Xid 13 entries in dmesg. Flagging for triage. @kevin can you take a look? :warning:

infra-bot: [ALERT] GPU THERMAL/POWER ANOMALY on gpu-wn-23. Metrics: gpu0_temp, gpu0_powercap. 95th latency increased +120ms. Dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood/graphs/gpu-wn-23

kevin: can you paste the `nvidia-smi -q -d POWER,TEMPERATURE` output and a short dmesg snippet? if it's spiking repeatedly we should drain it and replace from spare-pool.

sara: nvidia-smi output (latest):
```
GPU 0:
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp                     : 97 C
    Power Readings
        Power Draw                           : 243.67 W
        Power Limit                          : 250.00 W
        Enforced Power Limit                 : 180.00 W
```
and dmesg tail: `NVRM: Xid (0001:00): 13, pid=12345 pcie 0000:81:00.0` (repeats every ~2m)

kevin: Enforced power limit toggling to 180 suggests power capping from the host or driver fallback. Could be PSU sag or NV power limit reset. Is this rack PDU on auto-sense? Which topo?

oliver: Looking at telemetry: powercap toggles line up with the 95th latency spikes on the inference route pinned to that node. We had autoscale off for that pool yesterday to keep steady capacity — that's why the user traffic hit the hot node. Suggest immediate action: drain, failover, then hot-swap card if hw confirms.

mike: Hardware note: Xid 13 + thermal pattern often indicates GPU hitting thermal trip and then driver resets. Two possibilities: (1) fan/tach not spinning to spec (mechanical) or (2) PSU/bus causing power limit enforcement. Can we get `sensors` output and fan tach? Also check IPMI for PSU alarms.

sara: getting sensors + ipmi now. fan tach shows GPU0 fan at 3200 RPM then drops to 0 briefly before spinning back up. IPMI event log: no PSU fault entries.

kevin: ok plan: 1) drain gpu-wn-23 from pool right now: `rhctl drain gpu-wn-23 --reason "powercap oscillation / Xid13"` 2) move traffic to spare-pool-usw 3) repro on isolated maintenance node to see if card still hits powercap 4) if repro, schedule RMA or reseat.

infra-bot: `rhctl drain` job submitted by kevin at 08:26 UTC. State: draining -> in-flight.

oliver: also flip the node to power-limit 235W temporarily (if host path allows) to avoid abrupt resets while we observe. Keep caching and batching conservative for that pool.

mike: I'll request on-site tech to reseat GPU and check cooling shroud; if fan tach still drops after reseat we'll swap card. HW ETA 3 hours in us-west rack-12.

kevin: added runbook steps to the incident ticket: https://tickets.company/INC-9876. Steps include memtest stress, extended GPU burn (45m), and collect telemetry at 10s intervals.

sara: after drain, tail-latency dropped back to baseline immediately. Leaving node in maintenance mode. I'll attach full logs to the ticket.

oliver: good catch. follow-up: audit the pool autoscale setting — we should avoid pinning traffic to nodes with variable thermal headroom. I'll open a short doc with suggested autoscale/burst policies.

mike: HW will confirm reseat vs RMA and update ticket. If RMA, coordinate scheduled maintenance window with Product.

sara: tagging this resolved for now (pressure relieved). moving to maintenance. will update ticket once hw confirms. :white_check_mark:
